text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures on prod after turning on sessionAffinity for inference-service. Gateway is backed by an NLB -> k8s Service(type=LoadBalancer) -> pods. Some clients hit `tls: received record header too long` and others work fine. Anyone seen this pattern?

liam: that error usually means TLS client sent plaintext or the packet got routed to a non-TLS listener. Is TLS terminated at the gateway/NLB or at the pod? NLB default is L4 passthrough so pods should terminate TLS. :thinking_face:

maya: pods terminate TLS (we have certs in the pod/sidecar). But we recently toggled sessionAffinity: ClientIP on the k8s Service to keep KV cache warm. The failures started ~5m after the change.

alex: quick checklist: 1) externalTrafficPolicy on the Service? if it's Cluster it's doing SNAT and might break source IP expectations. 2) proxy protocol on NLB? If proxy-protocol is enabled but the pod/gateway isn't expecting it you'll see gibberish at TLS level. 3) target group type (instance vs ip) and healthcheck port.

jin: +1 on proxy protocol. Also ALBs can do cookie stickiness but NLB stickiness is connection/flow based. If you switched sessionAffinity to ClientIP, connections might be routed to a node that expects ProxyProtocol header.

maya: our Service annotation for NLB currently: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"` and we added `service.spec.sessionAffinity: ClientIP`. externalTrafficPolicy was default (Cluster). We did NOT enable proxy protocol.

liam: okay that narrows it. If externalTrafficPolicy is Cluster and ClientIP affinity is set, the kube-proxy hairpin/SNAT behavior might change the 4-tuple, causing the NLB to open new connections to different nodes mid-session. If the pod expects TLS handshake continuity (and session resumed), that could surface. For NLB+TLS you usually want externalTrafficPolicy: Local to preserve client IP and avoid SNAT.

alex: also double-check the Gateway/Service listener port mapping — if some backends are receiving ProxyProtocol v2 because of a previous config or an ELB attribute, they will see the extra bytes before TLS. Search ELB attributes for `proxy_protocol_v2`.

maya: doing a quick audit now. If we move to externalTrafficPolicy: Local, we need NodePort open on nodes and healthchecks to target nodeport. That ok for infra? @ops-bot can you confirm node security group allows the LB healthcheck ports to nodeports?

ops-bot: ops-bot: healthcheck from NLB (10.0.5.10) to nodes on ports 32000-32100 allowed in sg-prod-nodes. :white_check_mark:

jin: if you want a quick mitigation without rolling nodes, revert sessionAffinity to None and see if errors stop. Then test externalTrafficPolicy: Local in staging and enable sessionAffinity again.

maya: rolling back affinity for now. Also noticed some target groups had `protocol=TCP` vs `TLS`. For NLB we should be using TLS listener -> target group protocol TLS if we want TLS handled at target group? (confusing)

liam: NLB listener can be TLS and forward to TLS targets. If listener is TLS and target is TCP, NLB will terminate TLS on LB and speak plaintext to targets — that would definitely cause the pod to fail TLS handshake. So ensure listener/target protocol match.

alex: terraform snippet to check for ALB/target group stickiness (if you ever move to ALB):

```
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "tg" {
  name     = "my-tg"
  port     = 443
  protocol = "TLS"

  stickiness {
    enabled  = true
    type     = "lb_cookie"
    cookie_duration = 86400
  }
}
```

maya: good catch — I see two older LB listeners created by a prior infra change: one TLS listener forwarding to TG with protocol TCP. That explains the mismatch. I'll patch the listener to TLS->TLS or set target protocol TLS.

jin: after fix, re-enable sessionAffinity in staging with externalTrafficPolicy: Local and monitor. Also run `curl --resolve` from a client to reproduce handshake errors if any.

maya: plan: 1) rollback sessionAffinity in prod (done), 2) update LB listener -> ensure TLS->TLS, 3) test sessionAffinity + externalTrafficPolicy: Local in staging, 4) if green, roll to prod during low traffic window. I'll post updates. Thanks all. :pray:
